title: land merges a rebase conflict confined to one-line kb/_self doc hunks that two items edited at different words, so a sibling's doc row edit does not stop it at step rebase
goal: when the rebase of land stops only on kb/_self/*.md lines that both sides changed at different words (a table row or a one-line paragraph), land merges the line word by word keeping both sides, continues the rebase and says which lines it merged; a conflict on the same words, or in any other file, still stops it at step rebase

f=getattr(l,"merge_line_hunks",None)
b="| a | imports x and y, never z |";o="| a | imports x, y and w, never z |";t="| a | imports x and y, never z (always q) |"

import sys, os, io, subprocess, tempfile, contextlib
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import bl_land as L
f = getattr(L, 'rebase_merging_doc_rows', None)
ROW = '| a | imports x and y, never z |'
BASE = '# T\n\n' + ROW + '\n| b | other row |\n'
def land(path, main_line, work_line):
    t = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    g = lambda *a: subprocess.run(['git', *a], cwd=t, capture_output=True, text=True)
    g('init', '-q', '-b', 'main'); g('config', 'user.email', 'a@b.c'); g('config', 'user.name', 'n')
    p = os.path.join(t, path)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
    open(p, 'w').write(BASE); g('add', '-A'); g('commit', '-qm', 'base')
    g('checkout', '-qb', 'work'); open(p, 'w').write(BASE.replace(ROW, work_line)); g('commit', '-qam', 'work')
    g('checkout', '-q', 'main'); open(p, 'w').write(BASE.replace(ROW, main_line)); g('commit', '-qam', 'main')
    out = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
        r = f(t, 'main', 'work') if f else 1
    code = r if isinstance(r, int) else getattr(r, 'returncode', 1)
    g('checkout', '-q', 'work')
    return code, open(p).read(), out.getvalue()
M, W = '| a | imports x, y and w, never z |', '| a | imports x and y, never z (always q) |'
ok = land('kb/_self/tools.md', M, W)
same = land('kb/_self/tools.md', '| a | imports k |', '| a | imports m |')
other = land('kb/public/x.md', M, W)
print('different words in a _self doc row:', ok[0], '| same words:', same[0], '| other file:', other[0])
sys.exit(0 if ok[0] == 0 and '| a | imports x, y and w, never z (always q) |' in ok[1] and 'tools.md' in ok[2]
         and same[0] != 0 and other[0] != 0 else 1)

gates.question: Which hunks may the doc-row merge take, and which word changes count as different? (adjacent rows edited by two items form one git hunk)
options: one-line hunks only, touching words conflict

notes: SP-z3hyk4eh retrospective: three of nine landings stopped at step rebase (backlog.py ops: ST-zqbo7xgc 13:26, BG-wqc6sgug 13:30, ST-6tz7yhem 13:45, each land.step rebase exit=1): siblings edited different words of the same one-line rows of kb/_self/tools.md, backlog.md and code.md, which the rules treat as no overlap (backlog.md, Running a sprint: a shared doc orders no two items). The orchestrator resolved each by a word-level merge keeping both sides, by hand. The function name in the check is a proposal; the planner may rename it with the check. SP-xo45jvbj 2026-10-16: BG-yq2ojoiy's landing stopped at rebase on the one-line coord.py row of kb/_self/tools.md, which BG-wh3wardm had edited at other words; the orchestrator merged both inserts by hand. SP-6jfnx5i3 2026-10-17: again: BG-p2jcpxhl's landing stopped at rebase on the one-line coord.py row of kb/_self/tools.md, which ST-nlesmlru had edited at other words (KB_COORD_TOOLS=1); the orchestrator kept both by hand. Plan 2026-10-17: check 1 drives a real git rebase through bl_land.rebase_merging_doc_rows(root, upstream, branch) (a proposed name, as merge_line_hunks is) on three planted repositories: different words of a kb/_self row merge (exit 0, both edits kept, the merged file named in the output); the same words, and a kb/public file, stop (exit not 0).
